newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet adopts bill on pension rises.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet adopts bill on pension rises.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday approved a bill that would subject pension rises to negotiations on an annual basis and guarantee that they do not fall in real terms, Labour Minister Andrzej Baczkowski said.

"The pension increases would be subject to parliament's decision each year during the budgetary debate, but the increase would not be lower than the forecasted growth of prices of goods in a special basket," Baczkowski told a news briefing.

Baczkowski said the bill, sent to parliament as urgent, provides for increasing pensions twice a year in March and September, if annual inflation is higher than 10 percent, and also in June if inflation falls below 10 percent.
The bill is one of the first in a legislative package aimed at reforming Poland's inefficient social security system inherited from the Communist era.
Baczkowski said the next bills needed for the reform, including a crucial pension-fund bill, were likely to be submitted to parliament by the end of the year.
He said the pension-rising bill, due to take effect next year, would not embrace the military, police and other uniformed services, which would be covered by a special bill to be worked out by 1998.
Baczkowski said the pension-rising bill should guarantee a real-term pension increase of 1.5 percent next year.
